title: Mouse Vestibulo-Ocular Reflex Testing for Otolith Organs and Horizontal Semicircular Canal
author: Tong Zhao
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Stroke-physiological saline solution (Beyotime, catalog number: ST341-500 mL) Laboratory supplies

steps.title: Power on instrument and connect tablet
steps.instruction: Turn on the VOR instrument and wait 2–3 seconds for the camera to power up; then connect a tablet to the camera’s Wi‑Fi to display the real‑time image of the mouse eyes (pupils can be seen even in darkness).

steps.title: Fix mouse in noninvasive holder
steps.instruction: Wear gloves and a lab coat (heavy glove optional for older mice). Place the awake mouse on the holder base, then sequentially attach the neck holder, back holder, and nose holder to fix the head at ~30° nose‑down, ensuring the neck holder is not too tight and does not impede eye movement.

steps.title: Apply pilocarpine eye drops
steps.instruction: Using a 1 mL syringe, apply 1–2 µL of 0.5 % pilocarpine eye drops to each eye to induce pupil constriction; after miosis, gently wipe away excess drops with a soft tissue soaked in stroke‑physiological saline solution. Wait approximately 5 minutes for the drops to take effect before testing.

steps.title: Adjust camera focus and darken chamber
steps.instruction: Position the fixed, miotic mouse on the instrument, fine‑tune the camera distance in front, back, left, and right to obtain a clear, centered image of the eyes, then close the instrument lid and keep the mouse in the dark.

steps.title: Configure and run aVOR test
steps.instruction: On the instrument touch screen, set aVOR parameters: sinusoidal frequencies of 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.6, 3.2, and 5.0 Hz, peak velocity 40°/s, each stimulation lasting at least 50 cycles. Click start; the camera records eye movements for each profile in a separate video file.

steps.title: Configure and run OVAR test
steps.instruction: Set OVAR parameters on the touch screen: tilt the equipment to 17° or 30°, rotate the platform at constant velocities of 30, 50, or 80°/s in clockwise or counter‑clockwise direction, each stimulation lasting 2–3 minutes. Click start; eye movements are recorded in separate video files.

steps.title: Release mouse and return to cage
steps.instruction: After completing VOR measurements, open the nose holder, then the neck holder, and finally the back holder in sequence, and place the mouse back into its original cage. Note that the mouse remains miotic for ~30–40 minutes; if pupils dilate, re‑apply 1–2 µL pilocarpine eye drops.

steps.title: Download video recordings
steps.instruction: Automatically download the recorded eye‑movement videos via Wi‑Fi to a PC or edge‑computing device; processing generates an Excel file for each video containing eye‑trajectory data.

steps.title: Process eye movement data
steps.instruction: Open the eye‑movement data‑processing software, navigate to the folder with the Excel files, select either the aVOR or OVAR option, and let the software automatically calculate gain and phase for the chosen test.
